# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 5

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

I need to establish communication. Since I can speak to Mute and gesture to Deaf/Mute, I should try to get the layout of the wires from Deaf via gestures, or instructions from Mute via speech. However, without knowing which wire is which, I can't act yet.

Let's start by asking Mute for the general rule or status, as Mute has the manual. But Mute can't speak. I can only *hear* if someone speaks to me? No, the prompt says "You never receive gesture" and implies I am blind. Wait, the role description says: "When you speak, Mute receives it." It doesn't explicitly say who hears my speech. Usually, in these puzzles, Blind hears everyone except Deaf (who can't hear). So Blind hears Mute? No, Mute cannot speak. So Blind hears... nobody? Or does Blind hear the environment? The prompt says "Blind | Reach the bomb... Cannot See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed". It doesn't list "Hear" as a restriction for Blind. Deaf cannot hear. Mute cannot speak. So Blind likely hears Mute? No, Mute can't speak. Blind likely hears... well, if Mute can't speak and Deaf can't hear, who talks to Blind? Maybe Blind just acts on info passed through others?

Actually, let's look at the channels again.
"Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences."
This implies I can send info TO Mute and DEAF.
Who sends info TO ME?
Deaf can gesture. I cannot see gestures. So I don't get info from Deaf directly.
Mute can speak? No, Mute cannot speak.
So how do I get info?
Maybe I have to infer from the "Action Board" updates after actions?

Deaf sees the wires. Deaf can gesture. I can't see gestures.
Mute reads the manual. Mute can't speak.
Is there any way for Mute to communicate to me?
"When you speak, Mute receives it." -> This is outgoing.
What is incoming?
Usually, in these 3-person puzzles:
- Deaf sees visual cues. Can't hear.
- Mute reads text. Can't speak.
- Blind touches. Can't see.

Communication paths:
- Deaf can gesture to Mute (who can see gestures? The prompt says "Whoever can see receives it". Mute can see? Yes, Mute is not blind. Mute can read manual, so Mute can see text/gestures).
- Mute can... write? No, Mute can't touch.
- Can Mute speak? No.
- Can Deaf speak? No, Deaf can't hear, but can they speak? "Deaf | ... Cannot Hear anything". It doesn't say they can't speak. But usually "Deaf" implies no hearing, but they can talk. However, the prompt says "Speech is a voice... Whoever can hear receives your words". If Deaf can't hear, they don't receive words. But can Deaf *send* words? Yes, presumably. But who hears them? Blind and Mute? Mute can hear? "Mute | ... Cannot Speak". Doesn't say cannot hear. So Mute can hear. Blind can hear? "Blind | ... Cannot See". Doesn't say cannot hear. So Blind can hear.

So:
- Deaf can SPEAK (to Blind and Mute).
- Mute can HEAR (from Deaf and Blind).
- Blind can HEAR (from Deaf).

But Deaf cannot hear. So Deaf doesn't know what Mute/Blind say unless they gesture back?
And Mute cannot speak. So Mute communicates via... writing? No, Mute can't touch. Gesturing? Yes, Mute can gesture (hands are free).
Blind can gesture? Yes.

So the loop could be:
1. Deaf sees bomb. Deaf speaks to Blind/Mute describing the bomb.
2. Mute reads manual. Mute hears Deaf. Mute knows what to do. Mute gestures to Deaf/Blind? But Blind can't see gestures.
3. If Mute gestures to Deaf, Deaf sees it. Deaf can then speak to Blind telling him what to do.

This seems like the only path.
Step 1: I need Deaf to describe the bomb.
I can gesture to Deaf to ask for help?
Or I can speak to Mute? Mute can't speak.
I should probably signal that I am ready and waiting for instructions.

Since I don't know the state, I should wait for Deaf to speak first? But it's my turn.
If I do nothing, we stall.
I can gesture to Deaf. Deaf will see my gesture.
What gesture means "Tell me what to do"?
Maybe point to myself and then to the bomb?
Symbols: 👆 (point up), 🫵 (point at you), ✊ (fist).
I'll gesture to Deaf asking for information.

Also, I can speak to Mute. Mute can hear me. Mute can read the manual. Mute can gesture to Deaf.
So I can tell Mute: "Please coordinate with Deaf to guide me."
But Mute can't speak. Mute must gesture to Deaf. Deaf must speak to me.

Let's try to initiate this chain.
I will speak to Mute, asking them to relay instructions via Deaf.
And I will gesture to Deaf, indicating I need guidance.

Gesture to Deaf: I'll use symbols to indicate "Help" or "Info needed".
🤟 (ILY sign?) No.
Maybe ☝ (one finger) pointing to bomb?
Let's use simple symbols.
To Deaf: `["☝", "❓"]` - ❓ is not in alphabet.
Alphabet: 👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

`["👋", "🫵", "✋"]` - Hello, You, Stop/Wait?
Maybe just `["🫵", "☝"]` - You, Point Up (at bomb?).

To Mute: Speak clearly. "Mute, please check the manual. Use gestures to tell Deaf what to say to me. I cannot see gestures, so Deaf must speak the instructions to me."

```
speak(to="mute", text="Please read the manual. Coordinate with Deaf using gestures. Ask Deaf to verbally instruct me on which wire to cut based on the bomb's appearance.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵", "☝"])
```
